page: Amazon Web Services t3.large is a general-purpose, burstable virtual instance running on the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. Built upon the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core via hyper-threading. Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 33 MB L3 cache. It incorporates 8.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per virtual core. There is no bundled local storage or dedicated GPU accelerator, and network baseline throughput is rated at 1 Gbps.

Benchmark measurements reflect the burstable compute model and dual-thread limitation of a single physical core. The instance achieved a PassMark CPU score of 1939.37, while Geekbench returned 844.0 for single-core and 1034.0 for multi-core performance. In memory-intensive workloads, uncached large-block 256 MB read bandwidth reached 12.87 GB/sec alongside 10.63 GB/sec write bandwidth, with small-block cached reads reaching 93.13 GB/sec. Application testing yielded 1.57 million operations per second for Redis SET commands and 1.62 GB/sec for static web serving throughput.

Because the burstable CPU credit allocation limits sustained multi-core processing, resource saturation can throttle compute throughput under continuous intensive loads. The t3.large offers cost efficiency for low-to-moderate utilization profiles where full CPU cycles are required only intermittently. Suitable workloads include staging environments, low-traffic web applications, small microservices, and modest background utility tasks that benefit from 8.0 GB of RAM without demanding persistent heavy computation.

Configured with 2 vCPUs spanning a single physical core, the instance includes 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, offering a 1:4 compute-to-RAM ratio. It does not include local instance storage or GPU acceleration, and baseline network throughput is rated at 1 Gbps. Synthetic benchmarks reflect its burstable nature, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 1034.0, a PassMark CPU score of 1939.37, and a Redis SET throughput of 1.57 million operations per second. The instance delivers cost efficiency for workloads with fluctuating or intermittent CPU demands, making it appropriate for light web serving, microservices, development environments, and small background tasks.
